retrieved_context.text:
Penal Code, s.367
s.367: Theft. Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property
out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves
that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

Penal Code, s.380
s.380: Robbery. In all robbery there is either theft or extortion. Theft is
robbery if, in order to the committing of the theft, or in committing it,
or in carrying away or attempting to carry away property obtained by the
theft, the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause to any person
death or hurt or wrongful restraint.

Penal Code, s.431
s.431: House-trespass by night. Whoever commits house-trespass after sunset
and before sunrise is said to commit house-trespass by night.

Penal Code, s.327
s.327: Criminal force. Whoever intentionally uses force to any person,
without that person's consent, in order to the committing of any offence,
or intending by the use of such force to cause injury, fear or annoyance,
commits the offence of using criminal force.

Penal Code, s.294
s.294: Culpable homicide. Whoever causes death by doing an act with the
intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily
injury as is likely to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.

Penal Code, s.296
s.296: Culpable homicide amounting to murder. Culpable homicide is murder
where the act is done with the intention of causing death, or with the
intention of causing such bodily injury as the offender knows to be likely
to cause the death of the person to whom the harm is caused.

judgments silva v ag [Facts]
Facts:
The accused was convicted of theft of movable property contrary to section
367 of the Penal Code. At trial the prosecution relied on circumstantial
evidence and a confession. The accused appealed, arguing the confession was
involuntary and that the circumstantial evidence did not exclude every
reasonable hypothesis consistent with innocence.

judgments king v perera [Facts]
Facts:
The accused was charged with voluntarily causing grievous hurt contrary to
section 324 of the Penal Code following an altercation in a marketplace.
The victim suffered a fracture of the arm. The accused claimed the injury
resulted from a sudden quarrel and that he acted without premeditation and
in the heat of the moment.

judgments silva v ag [Reasoning]
Reasoning:
The Court reiterated that a confession must be voluntary to be admissible
under the Evidence Ordinance. Circumstantial evidence may found a
conviction only where it is consistent with guilt and inconsistent with any
reasonable hypothesis of innocence. The prosecution bears the burden
throughout.

judgments king v perera [Reasoning]
Reasoning:
The Court held that a fracture of a bone constitutes grievous hurt under
section 322. However, where the harm is inflicted in the course of a sudden
fight without premeditation, the case may fall within the mitigating
framework, and the court may temper the sentence accordingly. The burden
remains on the prosecution to establish the elements of the offence beyond
reasonable doubt.

judgments king v perera [Held]
Held:
Conviction under section 324 sustained, but the custodial sentence was
reduced in light of provocation and the absence of premeditation.
